scenes.line1: How does Git track your code?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how Git keeps your code organized and lets teams collaborate smoothly? Let's break down commits, branches, HEAD, and remote tracking.

scenes.label: Commit
scenes.sub: A commit is a snapshot of your code at a moment.
scenes.say: A commit is simply a snapshot of your code at a specific point in time. It marks progress and lets you roll back if needed.
Branches are pointers to commits, letting you develop features separately. HEAD is the reference to your current branch and commit—where new changes land.

scenes.title: Fetching Updates
scenes.say: Remote tracking branches show the state of branches on remote repositories. Use git fetch origin to update your local tracking branches.

scenes.question: What does HEAD point to?
scenes.wrong: HEAD points to the remote branch.
scenes.right: HEAD points to your current branch and commit.
scenes.say: Interview trap: HEAD does not point to the remote branch. It points to your current branch and commit. That's where new commits are added.
